comments.body:
## Refinement — the pattern has a MIRROR, and the criterion should cover both

Instance twelve arrived in the last minutes of the session, and it is the inverse of the other
eleven. An agent verifying that a signed close had reached `origin/tickets` — a check written
*because* of the hazard in `friendly-enervative-dikkops` — got:

```
COMPLETION_VERDICT  ABSENT  0 bytes
STATUS              ABSENT  0 bytes
SIGNATURE           ABSENT  0 bytes
```

which reads as a catastrophic finding: the close destroyed, exactly the disaster the check
existed to detect. It was **zsh not word-splitting an unquoted multi-line variable**, so
`git show` received one bogus path. Re-run with `while IFS= read -r`, every artifact was
present. The truth was the opposite of the report.

### Why this matters for the criterion as drafted

The ticket currently frames the defect as a check that produces its **passing** result for a
reason other than the condition it verifies. This instance shows the frame is one notch too
narrow. The same broken instrument can produce a confident **failing** result for a reason other
than the condition — and a false alarm is not harmless:

* it costs exactly the investigation the eleven fail-open cases cost, in the other direction;
* it is *more* likely to be believed, because an alarming result feels like diligence rewarded;
* acted on, it triggers recovery work against a store that was never damaged — and in this
  ticket's own subject area, "recovery" can mean raw git writes to a healthy tracker.

### Suggested amendment to the criterion

Broaden the reviewer prompt from "name every world in which this check PASSES" to:

> For each check the change adds or modifies, name every world in which it produces **any
> definite result** — pass or fail. If "the check never actually ran", "the instrument received
> the wrong input", or "the producer emitted nothing" is among them, the check cannot
> distinguish its verdict from its own failure.

The agent's own formulation, generalised from its earlier one, is the shortest statement of it:

> if you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence — an
> "everything is missing" result deserves the same suspicion as an "everything passed" one.

### Recursion worth noting for calibration

This is now the **third** time in this session that the shape appeared *inside work on the shape
itself*: a kill-matrix harness that reported all mutations surviving; a verification of a
`dikkops` exposure that was correct only by luck via cwd drift; and now a `dikkops`-motivated
check that reported total loss where there was none. Any calibration of this criterion should
expect the diagnostic tooling written to detect it to be a live source of instances.

comments.body: OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-21): the CONCEPT is approved. Placement question raised: does this fit as an addition to the existing code-review 'tests' criterion rather than a new criterion? Orchestrator finding: partially — the nine instances split into two populations, and only one is test code. Population 1 (five instances) was SHIPPED rebar code (gate scripts, pgrep patterns, silent lookup-miss paths); a tests-only placement misses it. Proposed disposition for the implementer: add the fail-open/producer-liveness detection language to the existing 'tests' criterion for the test-oracle population, and to the existing 'error-handling' criterion for the shipped-code population; do NOT create a new criterion unless calibration replay (the nine recorded instances) proves the pattern language cannot fire reliably from within those two hosts. Calibration AC from the ticket stands (fire on all nine pre-fix states, silent on post-fix).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A recurring defect shape — a check whose PASS/absent/empty result is indistinguishable from
the check never having run — appeared nine times in one session (2026-08-20/21). Code review
has no detection language for it. Per the refinement comment the mirror is included: a broken
instrument can also produce a confident FAILING result for a reason other than the condition,
so the language covers "any definite result", not just PASS.

**OPERATOR RULING (ticket comment, 2026-08-21): do NOT create a new criterion.** Add the
fail-open / producer-liveness language to the EXISTING `tests` criterion (test-oracle
population) and `error-handling` criterion (shipped-code population); a new criterion only if
calibration proves the language cannot fire from within those hosts.

### The nine instances (calibration corpus; full narratives in this ticket's comments)

`tests` host: (1) `sound-bumpkinly-thrush` — absence asserted on a child's output; a
signal-killed child writes nothing, so never-ran reports GREEN; (2) `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey`
— a convergence test re-derived the send path's dedup key instead of driving the send path;
(3) a harness grepped `"^FAILED"` against colorized pytest output — "0 failed" regardless;
(4) an orphaned sweep's truncated log and a clean log produce the same empty grep.

`error-handling` host: (5) `obvious-saline-gerbil` — health check never read the returncode;
(6) `defiable-distortive-pinniped` — `gen_env_registry` failed open on a helper missing from
`KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`; (7) `blocky-matricidal-squid` — the `os.environ` half, same posture;
(8) a `pgrep -f "make test"` monitor matched its own shell; (9) a `pgrep -f "review-plan"`
waiter matched its own process.

## Approach

Each host criterion's rubric already has a home:

- `tests`: the full rubric lives in the overlay prompt
  `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`. Add a **fail-open oracle** antipattern: an
  ABSENCE assertion (`not in`, `assert not`, `== ""`, empty-collection) derived from a
  subprocess/file/network/captured output, or a grep/regex over another tool's output used as a
  pass/fail signal, with NO liveness check on the producer (exit status, non-empty capture, an
  asserted presence). Litmus (the ticket's reviewer prompt, broadened per the refinement
  comment): *name every world in which the check produces its definite result — pass or fail;
  if "the producer never ran / emitted nothing" is among them, the check cannot distinguish its
  verdict from its own failure.* Qualify FP guard (iii) ("greps of COMMAND OUTPUT are valid") to
  require established producer liveness, and add the matching FP guard for absence assertions
  preceded by a liveness assertion.
- `error-handling` is a BASE-REVIEWER dimension (per its criteria_routing.json `_comment`), so
  its language goes in `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` §"Surface grounded
  findings": a short fail-open paragraph naming the shipped-code triggers — a silent
  lookup/membership MISS path, a subprocess check that never reads the returncode, a
  `pgrep`/`pkill` pattern that can match the matching process itself, any best-effort check
  whose failure is invisible — with the same litmus and the uniform remediation (assert the
  producer RAN before trusting any absence derived from it). The paragraph instructs the base
  reviewer to TAG such findings `error-handling` (so routing's error-handling @0.50 threshold
  hosts them), and delimits against the security overlay's existing same-named
  "fail-open error handling" antipattern (code-review-security.md): security-consequence
  fail-open (authz/validation fallback) stays with the security overlay; this language covers
  checks/oracles/health probes whose failure is invisible.
- Registry record: extend the `_comment` of the `tests` and `error-handling` entries in
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (this ticket + trigger list + placement
  ruling). No posture/threshold/blocking values change.
- Calibration corpus: add the nine instances as seeded-diff recall cases (pre-fix,
  `expect: finding`) each paired with a post-fix no-fire case (`expect: pass`) — instances 1–4
  in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`, 5–9 in
  `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-base.eval.yaml`, dso-corpus house style.
- Docs: code-review criteria have no per-criterion `rebar explain <id>` section (`_explain` in
  `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py` covers plan-review criteria + guides only); the code-review
  author surface is `rebar explain review` (`src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`).
  Default taken (see fork-record comment): document the pattern there with two worked examples
  (instances 1 and 6).

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` — fail-open oracle antipattern + FP guard.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — error-handling fail-open paragraph.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` — `_comment` provenance only.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — 4 recall + 4 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-base.eval.yaml` — 5 recall + 5 no-fire cases.
- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — pattern + two worked examples.

## Testing

- Offline (no model): `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py` — both extended specs must
  stay strict-clean (`validate_eval_spec(strict=True)`, registered scorers, every case has a
  `diff`).
- Live calibration replay (bedrock via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`): run each of the 18 new cases
  through its Pass-1 prompt via `rebar.llm.evals.eval_solver.run_case` (`code-review-tests` for
  1–4, `code-review-base` for 5–9). Decision rule, matching the `code_review_no_fire` scorer's
  presence/absence semantics: a pre-fix case passes iff it yields ≥1 finding; a post-fix case
  passes iff it yields ZERO findings. Fallback protocol when a post-fix case fires an UNRELATED
  finding (one whose claim is not about producer liveness / fail-open oracles): the seeded
  post-fix diff carries an incidental defect — revise the diff to remove it (keeping the
  liveness fix under test intact) and re-run until zero-finding; if the finding IS about
  producer liveness, the seeded fix is wrong — correct it and re-run. Every revision and final
  per-case result is recorded in the calibration ticket comment.
- FP posture: both hosts are ALREADY blocking (`tests` @0.54, `error-handling` @0.50), so no
  advisory ramp applies; the FP measurement is (a) the 9 post-fix no-fire cases and (b) the
  specs' standing no-fire families staying silent in the same replay. Record both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `code-review-tests.md` names the fail-open oracle antipattern with the producer-liveness
      litmus and matching FP guard; checked by `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [ ] `code-review-base.md` carries the error-handling fail-open language (silent lookup miss,
      unchecked returncode, pgrep self-match, invisible best-effort failure); checked by
      `rg fail-open` on the file.
- [ ] The `tests` and `error-handling` `_comment` fields in
      `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` record the triggers + this ticket; no
      routing VALUE changes (checked by diff).
- [ ] Calibration: all 9 pre-fix cases yield ≥1 finding and all 9 post-fix cases yield ZERO
      findings in the live replay (the `code_review_no_fire` presence/absence rule, with the
      unrelated-fire fallback protocol above); per-case results recorded as a ticket comment.
- [ ] FP posture recorded in the same comment (hosts already blocking; standing no-fire
      families silent).
- [ ] `rebar explain review` documents the pattern with ≥2 worked examples; checked by
      `rebar explain review | rg -c "fail-open"` ≥ 1 plus reading the examples.
- [ ] Eval specs strict-clean offline; checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py`.
